correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the invariant from its definition. It first proves \(\gamma_{tR}(\operatorname{Cr}_n)=6\) for every \(n\ge4\), then exhaustively classifies every weight-six function. The directed encoding of deleted edges gives exact survival criteria for both optimizer types. If all optimizers are killed, the zero-outdegree and zero-indegree sets force the bound \(|F|\ge n-1\). A concrete \(n-1\)-edge deletion pattern kills all optimizers while preserving minimum degree \(n-2\), and edge deletion cannot create a lower-weight total Roman dominating function. The packaged checker independently verifies definitions and optimizer sets for \(n=4,5\) and stress-tests the algebra and construction over larger finite ranges.
risks: The finite enumeration is corroborative only; the universal quantifier is justified by the analytic counting proof.

value.rationale: The result answers the new total-Roman-bondage invariant on the canonical one-factor perturbation of the complete bipartite graph. The initiating paper gives \(b_{tR}(K_{n,n})=n\), whereas the theorem proves that deleting one perfect matching changes the exact vulnerability to \(n-1\) for every \(n\ge4\).
